explanations.A: Correct. Substituting $k=5$ gives $|3x-10|>5$. This absolute inequality splits into two: $3x-10>5$ or $3x-10<-5$. Solving yields $x>5$ or $x<\frac{5}{3}$, which matches option A.
explanations.B: Incorrect. This option only includes the branch $x>5$ and omits the branch $x<\frac{5}{3}$.
explanations.C: Incorrect. This option gives the solution to $|3x-10|\le5$, i.e., the condition for the transaction *not* being flagged as high-risk.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This likely results from mistakenly using $|3x-k|>k$ instead of $|3x-2k|>k$ (forgetting the factor of 2), leading to $|3x-5|>5$ and solutions $x<0$ or $x>\frac{10}{3}$.
explanations.E: Incorrect. This likely results from mishandling the absolute value, e.g., interpreting $|3x-2k|$ as $|3x|-2k$, which gives $|3x|>3k$ and then $|x|>k$, so $x<-5$ or $x>5$.
